newsitem.title: USA: Murkowski opposes proposed $208 mln SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Murkowski opposes proposed $208 mln SPR oil sale.

text.p: The chairman of the Senate Energy Committee said Friday he opposed a sale of $207.5 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve approved by a Senate subcommittee earlier that day.

"Senator Murkowski continues to oppose the sale of $207.5 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve," his spokesman said. However the spokesman said at this point he did not know if the senator would try to block the sale when the bill reaches the Senate floor.
The Senate Interior Appropriations subcommittee approved the sale to cover the reserves operating costs for next year.
"I hope it's going to be the last time the subcommittee is going to finance the operation of the reserve in this manner," panel chairman Slade Gorton, a Washington Republican, said.

"But the constraints of the subcommittee's allocation and the dictates of the budget agreement and the expectations raised by the sale of oil in the House bill made it impossible to avoid another oil sale," Gorton said.
The House this week passed an interior spending bill that would sell $209 million of SPR oil next fiscal year.

Gorton said he would be willing to work with the Clinton administration and House members through the conference when the House and Senate versions of the bill are combined to avoid further oil sales.
But he said, "If we do so, it will come as a result of a very substantial reduction in programs and projects that are of interest to the members."
Gorton said he had talked with Energy Secretary Federico Pena on the matter this week.
The administration has said it opposed further sales of SPR oil and that its plan provided money to cover operating costs.
